summary_notes: Static analysis note: UUID candidates extracted from string pools or bytecode instructions are potential identifiers. Presence in a string pool or instruction is not proof of runtime use or active transmission.
Service registration note: A BLE API reference is not proof of server-side service registration or active GATT server establishment.
No UUID is marked as registered in Phase 2; all extracted UUIDs represent static candidates without registration verdicts.

Scope limitation: Analysis relies on DEX string pools, method reference tables, and const-string instruction inspection. Full program slicing and inter-procedural data-flow analysis are not performed.

Known false-positive sources: Standalone 4-character hex strings in DEX string pools (e.g. '0000', 'dead', 'fade') match 16-bit Bluetooth UUID syntax but may represent arbitrary string constants, dates, or hash fragments unless matched with known Bluetooth SIG assigned numbers or BLE API call sites.

findings.diagnosis: UUID candidate '0000180d-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb' discovered in DEX constants/strings, but has no static data-flow link to BluetoothGattService constructor or BluetoothGattServer.addService() registration call sites.

blind_spots_and_limitations: Cross-Method Data Flow: BluetoothGattService objects constructed in helper/factory methods and passed across method boundaries to addService() are classified as REGISTRATION_PATTERN_UUID_UNRESOLVED because inter-procedural data-flow slicing is not performed.

Field-Based Storage: Services or UUIDs stored in instance/static fields (e.g. this.mService) and subsequently registered in separate lifecycle methods are classified as REGISTRATION_PATTERN_UUID_UNRESOLVED (FIELD_BASED_SERVICE_OBJECT).
Dynamic and Obfuscated UUIDs: UUID values generated at runtime via string concatenation, byte arrays, reflection, or UUID.randomUUID() cannot be resolved to static string literals.

Control-Flow Sensitivity: Intra-method tracing models forward register simulation; complex branching where registers are redefined on alternative paths falls back safely to REGISTRATION_PATTERN_UUID_UNRESOLVED.

Non-Standard Wrapper Frameworks: Third-party reactive or proprietary BLE vendor SDKs that encapsulate BluetoothGattServer internally without calling standard Android framework APIs directly are not tracked.

findings.explanation: Matches official Bluetooth SIG assigned specification 'Heart Rate Service' (https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/assigned-numbers/). Standard protocol identifier; not indicative of conflict or malicious intent. Analyst note: Standard GATT Heart Rate Service (16-bit 0x180D) widely used by health, fitness wearables, and chest straps.

limitations: Definition of Strong Duplicate Static Registration: An assessment is classified as STRONG_DUPLICATE_STATIC_REGISTRATION (with is_proven = true strictly according to UCSD's static-analysis evidence criteria) if and only if two or more distinct APK packages both demonstrate verified intra-method Dalvik register data-flow (STRONG_STATIC_ASSOCIATION) associating the identical GATT service UUID with BluetoothGattServer.addService(). Static analysis establishes high-confidence static overlap; it does NOT constitute proof of runtime vulnerability, confirmed host collision, or confirmed service squatting.

Duplicate Candidates are NOT Proven Conflicts: Identical UUID candidate strings appearing across multiple APKs (e.g. from shared third-party SDKs, utility libraries, or string pools) without verified dual static GATT registration are classified as DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_NO_REGISTRATION. They are explicitly NOT presented as runtime service conflicts.

Non-Malicious Nature of Assigned Standards: Matching a Bluetooth SIG assigned UUID (e.g. Heart Rate, Battery Service) or known vendor identifier is a standard protocol implementation pattern. It does NOT indicate malicious intent or spoofing without operational device evidence.

No Unverifiable System/Vendor Claims: An identifier is classified as system-level or vendor-specific (KNOWN_SYSTEM_OR_VENDOR_MATCH) only when supported by verifiable source documentation in the versioned knowledge base.

Strict Absence of Calibrated Probabilities: Conflict determinations are discrete qualitative classifications based on verified static Dalvik bytecode evidence, not numeric risk scores or calibrated percentages.
Knowledge Base Scope and Currency: The UUID knowledge base contains curated identifiers with verifiable provenance. Unknown UUIDs remain strictly unknown (UNKNOWN_UNCONFLICTED).
Presence in DEX string pool is not proof of runtime execution or active service advertisement.
Intra-method tracing verifies Dalvik register data flow to BluetoothGattServer.addService(); it does not cover cross-method parameters, dynamic reflection, or native code.
UUID knowledge base lookup performs exact matching against curated public specifications with verifiable provenance. Unknown UUIDs remain strictly unknown.
Categorical evidence levels are qualitative static findings and do not represent calibrated runtime probabilities or risk scores.
Static analysis cannot prove runtime host-level vulnerability or confirmed service squatting without operational device execution.
